Subject : Reservoir Fluid Study, Dulang A-14 Well
                Our Ref: MFL 20100151

Three (3) separator gas, one (1) separator condensate and two (2) stock tank water samples were collected from Dulang A-14 well and were forwarded to our Kuala Lumpur laboratory for quality checking prior performing further reservoir fluid analysis. 

Core Laboratories Malaysia Sdn. Bhd. appreciates this opportunity to have been of service to PETRONAS Carigali Sdn. Bhd. (PCSB). Samples Received
Three (3) separator gas, one (1) separator condensate and two (2) stock tank water samples were collected from Dulang A-14 well and forwarded to our Kuala Lumpur laboratory for quality checking prior performing further reservoir fluid analysis. 

SEPARATOR SAMPLES

Surface Sample Validation (Separator Condensate)
The separator condensate sample was heated to a temperature of 200°F prior to any sample removal in order to eliminate any possible wax precipitation. Upon heating, the  water and mud  amounts in the sample were determined as a quality check. The samples were then transferred into Corelab cylinders prior further analysis and the original cylinders were returned to Halliburton. 

Bubble Point Determination (Separator Condensate)
A portion of separator condensate  sample was charged to a high pressure visual PVT cell. Since the separator temperature was reported to be below ambient laboratory temperature, the saturation point determination was performed at ambient laboratory temperature (~ 70°F).

Surface Sample Validation (Separator Gas)
The separator gas samples were agitated well and allowed to stabilized at a temperature 20°F above the separator temperature. The opening pressure and amount of mud and water were then determined from the validation process. The samples were then transferred into Corelab cylinders and the original cylinders were returned to Halliburton. The hydrocarbon composition through C12+ was then determined prior further analysis. 

Sample Composition by Flash Separation
The composition of the separator condensate sample was determined using a flash separation technique and gas chromatography. The separator condensate sample was flashed at atmospheric pressure and a controlled temperature of 120°F and separated into gas and liquid phases.  The gas was analysed by extended gas analysis technique  and the liquid by temperature programmed  high resolution capillary gas chromatography.  The two analyses were then mathematically recombined to the flash gas-liquid ratio. The schematic diagram of flash separation technique is presented as Figure 2 on page A.4 of this report. 

Sample Selection
A representative of PETRONAS Carigali Sdn. Bhd. has selected sample pair from Cyl# 4878 (separator gas) and Cyl# 819614 (separator condensate) for wellstream composition calculation, physical recombination and further PVT study.

Wellstream Composition Calculation
The measured compositions of the selected separator gas and separator condensate were used, in conjunction with the corrected field gas-oil ratio, to calculate the reservoir fluid composition and the recombination ratio.  

Shrinkage Measurement
The shrinkage measurement was performed on separator condensate (Cyl# 819614) to correct the separator liquid flowrate at stocktank condition as provided in the sampling datasheet to the separator liquid flowrate at reported separator conditions. The shrinkage calculation requires a relative volume which was obtained from a partial constant compositon expansion (CCE) test. 

Since the separator condensate sample was collected at separator temperature below the ambient laboratory temperature, the partial CCE test was performed at various temperature of 80°F, 100°F & 120°F. The relative volume obtained from these various temperatures of partial CCE test were extrapolated to provide the relative volume at reported separator temperature. The extraplorated relative volume at separator temperature was used for shrinkage calculations.

WATER SAMPLES

Sample Selection
A representative of PETRONAS Carigali Sdn. Bhd. has requested Corelab to perform  API 12 ion Water Analysis, Resistivity, pH, Specific Gravity, Total Dissolved Solids and Scaling Potential analyses on both stock tank water samples (collected at 18:30 hrs and 18:00 hrs).

Water Compositional Analysis
Salinity
Conductivity and salinity measures waters ability to conduct electricity, which provides a measure of what is dissolved in water. Salinity is estimated from conductivity measurement. Since salts in water conduct current, conductivity is proportional to the salt-concentration. A complex mathematical equation is utilized to calculate or estimate salinity from conductivity. This equation accounts for the temperature dependence of conductivity.

Elemental Analysis 
The sample was filtered through a Whatman No. 5 filter paper and a dilution was made, using distilled water, according to their salinity. This is to ensure that all the elements are in the correct range for ICP analysis.  The result was presented in mg/l on the ICP (Inductively Coupled Plasma Atomic Emission Spectroscopy) for all detectable elements found in formation waters, seawaters and drilling fluids. A routine water analysis consists of determining the following ions by ICP technique – sodium, potassium, calcium, magnesium, barium, strontium, dissolved iron, sulphate (as total sulphur), phosphorus, silicon, boron, aluminium and lithium.

Chloride Content
The diluted sample was then analysed for chloride content by titration with silver nitrate solution using an ion selective electrode. Before usage, the instrument was calibrated by running a quality control sample.

pH / Bicarbonate / Carbonate Determinations
pH and bicarbonate determinations were performed by ion selective electrode. The instrument was first calibrated using pH 10, 7 and 4 buffers and checked by using a bicarbonate quality control sample. The pH and bicarbonate determinations was performed on filtered undiluted sample. The pH of a sample was initially determined using an ion selective electrode.  If pH is above 8.1, the sample is titrated with sulphuric acid for carbonate down to pH 8.1 then down to pH 4.1 for bicarbonate.

Total Iron Determinations
The measurement was performed on unfiltered & undiluted sample.  A 10ml aliquot of water was sub-sampled and heated on a hotplate after the addition of hydrochloric acid.  The sample was filtered into a 100 ml flask and made up to the mark with distilled water (x 10 dilution). The sample was then read on the ICP for total iron concentration.

Specific Gravity & Density
This analysis was performed using a density meter on a filtered & undiluted sample. The temperature was set at 15.6°C and the specific gravity was reported at 60°F. 

Resistivity Determinations
The  resistivity determination was performed on filtered & undiluted sample using a null point method and noting the temperature reading.  The resistivity was reported as a calculated value at 60°F.

Physical Recombination
Large volume of selected separator gas and separator condensate were physically recombined to the calculated recombination ratio of standard cubic feet of primary separator gas at 14.73 psia and 60ºF, per barrel of primary separator liquid at separator conditions. The recombined reservoir fluid sample (Cyl# TS 75403) was then subjected to saturation pressure determination and compositional analysis. 

Recombined Reservoir Fluid Sample Composition by Cryogenic Distillation
The composition of the recombined reservoir fluid sample was determined using cryogenic distillation and gas/liquid chromatography techniques. The schematic diagram of cryogenic distillation is presented as Figure 1 on page A.4 of this report. 
The   recombined reservoir fluid sample was pumped from the cylinder into a pre-weighed flask submerged in liquid nitrogen (-176°C) and the sample allowed to warm slowly. The pressure in the flask rises as the light-ends begin to vaporise. The gas phase in the cryo flask was then transferred into a pre-weighed, pre-evacuated single-ended Hoke cylinder (toepler). The cryo flask was then warmed slightly in a water bath (~ 30°C) to complete the distillation process. The final weights of these receivers were taken (once at room temperature) and the contents submitted for GC analysis. See below (Gas Compositions and Stablised Liquid Compositions) for detailed explanation on gas chromatography techniques.These compositions were then combined mathematically, to the measured gas-liquid weight ratio to calculate the recombined reservoir fluid compositions.

COMPOSITIONAL ANALYSIS

Gas Compositions
Gas compositions were determined using extended gas chromatography by the GPA 2286 method using a multi-column gas chromatograph system.  A single partial pressure charge was passed through the sampling valve and charged to each analytical column. The TCD (Thermal Conductivity Detector) reads O2, N2 and C1 from the molecular sieve column followed by C2, CO2, C3, iC4, nC4, iC5, nC5 from the porous polymer column. The FID (Flame Ionization Detector) reads up to Cn+ from the capillary column independently.   A temperature programme was used in order to provide optimum detection and resolution of the dodecanes plus components. 

Stabilised Liquid Compositions
Liquid compositions were determined by high resolution capillary gas chromatography utilising a cold-on-column injection technique. This injection technique involved the sample being deposited directly onto the front end of a wide bore capillary column. The sample was injected cold (35°C) to eliminate flashback through the injector port. Once the injection was completed, the front end of the column was rapidly heated to 300°C to vapourise the sample. The various constituents of the sample then elute through  column at different retention times into a Flame Ionisation Detector (FID). The output or signal of the detector is proportional to the amount of a component or constituent present in the sample. Note that the FID response is proportional to the number of the carbon atoms, therefore the FID can be regarded as a mass detector.

PARTIAL GAS CONDENSATE STUDY (Recombined Reservoir Fluid Sample, Cyl# TS 75403)

Constant Composition Expansion (CCE)
Constant Composition Expansion (CCE) was carried out in a high pressure visual PVT cell.  A portion of the recombined reservoir fluid sample was charged to the PVT cell at reservoir temperature.  A constant composition expansion was then performed during which the dew point pressure was determined and retrograde liquid build up was measured until a maximum volume was reached.  Pressure-volume data for the single phase and two phase fluid were also obtained.

The deviation factor, Z,  was determined by pumping known volumes of the fluid from the PVT cell at 5000 psig and measuring the gas volumes at standard conditions.  The deviation factors were then calculated for the other pressures using the measured relative volumes from the above expansion test.  

Retrograde Liquid Curve (RLC) Measurement
Retrograde liquid curve (RLC) measurement was performed on the recombined reservoir fluid sample where the liquid build up at each depletion pressure stage was measured and expressed as a percentage of the sample volume at dew point pressure. From this analysis, the pressure stage where the maximum liquid build up was obtained can be determined.

During the RLC measurement, there was evidence of liquid drop out present below the saturation pressure. However this liquid drop out was insignificant and unable to be quantified.

Based on this observation, Constant Volume Depletion (CVD) was not performed on this sample.
